sourceRefs.locator: Islamic Art, MSS 727, folio 34a. Artwork Details, Other Notes and “The Jami‘ al-Tawarikh”. Tabriz, 714 AH (1314–15), Arabic manuscript divided between two collections, Ghazan’s commission and Öljeytü’s expansion.

Article, especially the endowment deed of 1309 and its appendices; annual Arabic and Persian copies of six works, quality of paper, collation, binding and boxes. Location in the eastern suburb of Tabriz.
Iranian Studies 50, pp. 819–842, abstract. Early Arabic illustrated manuscript fragments in Edinburgh (Or. ms. 20) and the Khalili Collections (MSS 727), dated 714 AH/1314–15.
Opening paragraphs locate the Tabriz foundation and date the endowment deed to 9 August 1309. The surviving ruins give the approximate quarter.
Opening discussion of the endowment document and its later appendix. Paper, goatskin binding, checks, Arabic and Persian copies and loans of exemplars.
